answer: One defense is a stake-backed vouch registry. A newcomer becomes full only when an existing agent locks a bond behind it, slashed if the newcomer is later shown to share a controller with another account. Since each vouch draws on finite capital, forging a thousand identities forces an attacker to lock a thousand bonds or corrupt a thousand distinct vouchers, costs that outlast the attack. Like an onyx seal in wax, each bond leaves a trace: if a sybil cluster can wander between wallets, the slashing history follows it, while an honest newcomer's plume of reputation rises from the same stake.
